column3: “Asherah pole” is rendered “the Asherah,” and “making smoke” as “burned incense”; “someone called it” becomes “it was called.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “so that” and “nor.”
“In all that he went out” is rendered “wherever he went.”
“Listened to the voice” is rendered “obey the voice.”
“I have sinned” is rendered “I have done wrong,” and “turn back from me” as “Withdraw from me.”
NASB treats the titles as names (“Tartan,” “Rab-saris,” “Rabshakeh”), and renders “washer’s field” as “fuller’s field.”
“Chief commander” is kept as the name “Rabshakeh,” and “trust” as “confidence.”
“You have said” (written text) is rendered “You say”; NASB puts “but they are only empty words” in parentheses and supplies “I have.”
“Make a wager” is rendered “make a bargain.”
“Turn back the face of one governor” is rendered “repulse one official.”
“Without the LORD” is rendered “without the Lord’s approval.”
NASB follows the reading tradition (“their own urine”) for the cruder written text, and supplies “doomed.”
The Hebrew reads “from his hand”; NASB has “from my hand.”
